Accounting Dashboard: Implementation Spec

Everything an engineer needs to build the dashboard and its widgets correctly: design tokens, responsive grid, the three widget sizes, resize reflow, the add-widget flow, overlays, and accessibility. All visual values resolve from the Pathway Design System tokens, not hand-authored values.

open_in_newFigma: design source (placeholder) descriptionWidget-by-widget docs: SharePoint (placeholder)

1. Design tokens

All colour, spacing, radius, border, type and motion come from the Pathway Design System, loaded over CDN from the published package. Source of truth: github.com/helloimjolopez-collab/pathway-ds · package @helloimjolopez-pathway/pathway-tokens@10.0.4.

  • Primitives (--primitive-color-{family}-{step}): the raw ramps (cool-neutral, warm-neutral, brand, amethyst, red, green, saffron, orange, and the accent families). Alpha variants on anchor steps (e.g. --primitive-color-green-350-16) for tints; steps 4/8/16/24/36/50/70.
  • Semantics (--semantic-color-{fill|foreground|stroke}-*): role tokens. Surfaces are warm (widget/header = fill-static-neutral-faint, warm-neutral-0 #fefefd), text is cool grey (foreground-static-neutral-*), canvas = fill-surface-canvas (cool-neutral-10 #fafafa).
  • Rule: semantic where a role fits, primitive only where no semantic exists (categorical chart series, alpha scrims/shadows). Nothing wears a raw hex.

Motion

Easing from DS: --motion-easing-standard (enter/most), --motion-easing-decelerate (overlays). Durations 150ms (micro) / 300ms (enter). Respects prefers-reduced-motion.

Elevation

DS --elevation-widget / sheet / lift / overlay for card and overlay shadows (never hand-rolled rgba).

2. Responsive grid

The dashboard is a CSS grid whose column count is driven by container width (@container on .dashboard), so it responds to the content area, not the viewport.

Container widthColumnsMin col
< 720px460px
≥ 720px876px
≥ 1050px12fluid (Explore min 1050)

This is the Pathway Grid from Figma: 12 columns, gutter 16, inside the SheetContainer and Sheet padding (56 each side at desktop). grid-auto-rows: 8px, gap: 16px (gap-base), grid-auto-flow: row. Widgets span whole columns/rows; a span of n rows is 24n - 16 tall, which draws Figma's heights exactly: 176 for Glance, 416 for Detail and Explore.

3. Widget sizes

Three sizes, named as in the Figma Widget component set: Glance (kpi), Detail (wide), Explore (xwide), plus Band (the full-width Financial KPIs). Column span adapts to the current column count; row span is fixed per size.

Size4-col8-col12-colRowsRole
Glance (kpi)span 4span 4span 4; span 3 once the grid is ≥ 1148 (3 columns ≥ 275)8 (176px)Headline metric + the one actionable number; hover "View details" drills to Detail without resizing.
Detail (wide)span 4span 8span 618 (416px)Table or chart with controls (filter, sort, view toggle, search).
Explore (xwide)span 4span 8span 1218 (416px)Table + chart side by side; fullest in-grid view.
Bandfull row (1 / -1)8 (176px)Full-width KPI band; single size only.

4. Resize reflow

When a widget is resized, or the container crosses a breakpoint, its size is clamped to the current column cap (fitSize() against curCap()): a widget can never request more columns than the grid currently offers, so it never overflows the viewport or pushes content off-screen. The grid then re-places following widgets automatically (grid-auto-flow: row). On an explicit resize, the widget is scrolled back into view (scrollIntoView, centered) so the user stays oriented. Cap mapping: content width ≥1050 → Explore allowed; ≥566 → Detail; else Glance.

5. Add-widget & manage flow

  • Edit dashboard (in the dashboard name dropdown) enters manage mode: every widget gets a drag-to-move handle, plus resize / duplicate / remove, and the dashboard name becomes editable. Done exits.
  • Add widget opens a catalog: a category rail (with counts), a searchable list/tile view, an accurate glance-size preview of each widget, an Add / Added state per card, and a module badge (AP/AR/GL/PR/FA/PO). Done confirms with a toast: single → "[Widget] has been added to the dashboard"; multiple → "N widgets added to the dashboard".
  • Swap: a widget's header chevron opens a searchable list to swap it for another widget, keeping its current size.
  • An "Add widget" affordance is always available at the end of the dashboard.

6. Overlays

All focus/detail overlays share one canonical size: width: min(960px, 94vw), height: min(86vh, 680px), fixed height with the body scrolling internally, so an overlay never resizes or jumps as its content re-renders. The scrim has no re-entrance animation. Small confirm/picker dialogs are a separate compact class. Every overlay states its subject once (no header/footer duplication), uses one table pattern with cells aligned under headers, status as icon+text badges (never colour alone), and a single clear action hierarchy. Per-row actions sit inline; bulk actions (e.g. Export) live with the selection summary in the toolbar.

7. Accessibility

  • Colour contrast from the semantic foreground tokens meets WCAG AA for text; status is never communicated by colour alone, always icon + text.
  • Focus uses the DS focus ring (--semantic-color-stroke-focusring-base, 2px, 2px offset) on all interactive elements.
  • Keyboard: all controls reachable and operable; checkboxes/toggles expose role + aria-checked/aria-pressed; menus use aria-haspopup/aria-expanded.
  • Screen reader: each row has an aria-label summarising its data and action; live region announces status changes.
  • Motion: honours prefers-reduced-motion. Touch: hover-only affordances (e.g. copy) reveal on tap where there is no hover.
  • Interactive elements look interactive; static context never looks tappable.

8. What changes / is unavailable at smaller sizes

  • Add-widget / manage flow: desktop only, disabled below 900px (the catalog needs the rail + grid + preview). Tablet and below show a hint instead.
  • Column reflow: 12 → 8 → 4 columns as the container narrows; widgets clamp Explore → Detail → Glance so nothing overflows.
  • Overlays go full-screen on small viewports.
